notes: Captain Brannoc Hale (bible 5.2), the whole Watch of Briar Glen plus two teenagers with spears. Honest, tired, rumpled; clipped sentences, counts doors. Fears he is too old for this. SECRET: he sleepwalks and hides the mine dust on his boots. AC-3/bible: he must not know he delivered the 'friend below' note until The Captain's Boots reveals it, so every line about the note is behind hale.sleepwalking.revealed (the entry boots-acknowledged and the option ask-note); before that he only deflects about his boots. The quest owns hale.secret.kept / hale.secret.exposed (tell the town or keep it). Also: the missing-persons list, the jail (hale.jailed, set by the theft system; the loose stone is only hinted), Act III testimony (a persuasion check unless the secret was kept), and a reaction to each headline ending. Disposition: cold (<= -10) shuts him down; >= 10 he admits the dust on his boots.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Well met. A knight in Briar Glen, and I've been the entire Watch for twenty years. Captain Hale. Sit, if the stool takes you. I'd stand, but my knees have views.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Scout the tree line for me, would you? My knees don't do tree lines. Captain Hale, what's left of the Watch. You're the archer, I take it. I'm told you hit things.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Ah. Sorcerer. Right. Civil of you to come to the Watch House first. Could you, ah, do something about the dreams? Everyone's having them. I'm told it's the damp.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I know what you are. Don't make me prove it. Hale, Captain. Keep your hands where I can count them; I'm told I count badly.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Captain Hale, Briar Glen Watch. Such as it is: me, two lads with spears and a kettle. State your business, then sit. You're making the lads nervous.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Back. Good. Come in, mind the kettle. Anything new?

options.text: Can I see the missing-persons list?
You look like you haven't slept.
I want to talk about the note.
Captain. Tell me what you need.
I can look into the dreams.
Will you stand with me before the council?

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Mind the doors on your way. I count them.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Three weeks. Seven beds gone cold. I've started counting the doors on my rounds, like that'll help.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Moss Greaves, tanner. Ettie Lark, milkmaid. Rowan Tate and Harlan Burr, miners. Mina Coles, schoolhouse. Fitch, from the Ox. And the Pell girl, Tansy, the night you arrived.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I've written it all down. Take a copy. Where their footprints stopped, I've marked on the map. All toward the mine. Every one of them.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Cobbles, then the mine road, then gravel, then nothing. Bare feet, every one; not a shoe among them. They stop at the gate. Barred, on Vane's order. And Vane chairs the council.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The Watch is me, two lads who ask leave to visit their mothers, and a kettle. Before you say it: yes. I'm too old for this. Everyone knows. Strike that from the record.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Dust. It's a mining town. It gets into everything. Don't write that down.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I haven't. Not properly. I go to bed one man and wake another, and my boots are dusty with mine dust. I've never been up the mine road, not since the gate shut. I tie the laces to the bedpost now.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: They're still tied in the morning. That's the part I can't explain. Tell no one. If the council hears, Vane gets the Watch.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: So. The note under your door. It was my boots that took it. Eyes shut, boots on, up the Ox's stairs and under the door, and not a notion in my head. I've sat here an hour working out how to say it.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: You kept it between us. I won't forget that, and neither will my knees. If you've a use for an old man who owes you, I'm yours.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The town knows now. Vane's got the council's ear and the Watch is half his. I don't hold it against you. I'd have told, in your place. I'd only have hoped I wouldn't.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I carried it. In my sleep. A stranger wrote it and my feet delivered it, like the world's worst postman. 'The beast keeps them in the dark.' Who taught my feet to follow a stranger?

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Whoever it was, they know the way, they know me, and they know who'll listen. Find them. I'll tie myself to the bedpost if you like.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Peer to peer, then. Watch the mine gate at dusk. Be a second pair of eyes on the road. And tell me, now and then, that I haven't lost my wits. You'll do for all three.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Bless you. East of the bridge, where the Briarwood comes down to the road. The footprints all head for the gate; I want to know if anything comes out. Report to me. Not to Vane.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Can you? Everyone has the same one. A music, a long way off, and a door. I don't. I want that on record. I don't have it.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: ...You're right. I've nothing. A feeling in my knees. Get out of my sight before I find something to charge you with.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Pockets. Out. All of them. (He finds a tin.) Is that my own tobacco? Take it. I'll pretend I never saw. Clear out before I recall otherwise.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Before the council, to speak for what's below. They'll want proof and they'll want a name to blame. I'm one old man with a badge. Let me think what it costs me.

modifiers.label: The town has laughed at him

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I'll stand. I've stood in worse rooms, though never one with Vane in it. Say what you saw; I'll say what I saw, and I'll say you don't lie. That's worth more than my name.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I can't, not today. Bring me something I can put on a table, and I'll stand beside it. That isn't cowardice. It's a captain's arithmetic.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I've nothing to say to you. Not until you've shown me something other than your back.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: We'll see. Actions, not words. I've heard words.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Good. Mind the door.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Caught with your fingers in someone else's pocket. I don't enjoy this. The cell's older than the Watch and damper than the river. You'll sit in it till the sun's up and think about what you've done.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Nothing in there but a bench, a bucket and the damp. Nobody's looked at that floor in a hundred years, and I'm not going to start tonight.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: I believe you. Doesn't change the bench. Make it right with whoever you wronged, and we'll call it done.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: A misunderstanding in somebody's pocket. Sit. We'll talk when the bench has had its say.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Door closes. Don't kick it; it's older than your grandmother.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (Hale stands at the Watch House door, eyes shut, boots dusty. He is counting under his breath.) 'Forty. Forty-one. All the doors. Someone has to count the doors.'

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: (The lamp over the Watch House door is still lit.)

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: Seven doors, counted twice. All open, all lit, all the beds warm. I slept. Eleven hours. I woke with clean boots. You'll not know what that is to me. Thank you.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The bell rings each dusk. I find I'm on the bridge for it, every time. I've told the lads it's duty.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: They're home. All seven. And a creature that carried them gently lies dead. I wrote the report. I didn't know what to put under 'thanks to'. I put his name in. I hope you don't mind.

nodes.speaker: hale
nodes.text: The bounty's paid and the council's pleased. I haven't written the report. Don't ask me to. Vane's quite right that nobody wants to read it. Somebody ought to.
